sections.heading: Quick Verdict
sections.markdown:
## Quick Verdict: Which Active Ingredient Should You Pick?

Drinking 2 cups of organic Spearmint Tea (Mentha spicata) daily reduces free testosterone levels by up to 30%, making it an effective natural anti-androgen for PCOS jawline breakouts.

sections.heading: Comparison Methodology
sections.markdown:
## Dermatological Comparison & Action Mechanisms

Elevated free testosterone and DHT stimulate facial oil glands to produce thick sebum along the chin and jawline. Spearmint tea polyphenols decrease circulating free androgens.

Dermatological Comparison & Action Mechanisms

sections.heading: Decision Criteria
sections.markdown:
## Decision Criteria for Indian Skin Types

Ideal for women experiencing pre-menstrual acne flare-ups in the luteal phase or PCOS jawline cysts. Not recommended for pregnant women or individuals with severe acid reflux.

sections.heading: Side By Side Matrix
sections.markdown:
## Side-by-Side Comparison Matrix

Spearmint Tea (Mentha spicata) lowers free testosterone up to 30% for hormonal cysts. Peppermint Tea (Mentha piperita) contains high menthol and focuses on digestive comfort.

| Parameter | Spearmint Tea (Mentha spicata) | Peppermint Tea (Mentha piperita) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Anti-Androgen Effect | Proven (Lowers free testosterone up to 30%) | Minimal to None |
| Key Component | Carvone & Rosmarinic Acid | High Menthol |
| Acne Target | Jawline & PCOS hormonal cysts | Digestive soothing only |
| Daily Dosage | 2 cups per day (Morning & Evening) | As desired |

Side-by-Side Comparison Matrix

sections.heading: Reader Fit Tradeoffs
sections.markdown:
## How To Layer Both Actives Safely

Steep 1 tea bag or 2.5g loose spearmint leaves in hot water for 7-10 minutes. Consume 1 cup in the morning and 1 cup in the evening consistently for 6-8 weeks.

How To Layer Both Actives Safely

sections.markdown:
## Clinical Safety & Dermatologist Notes

Reviewed by Board-Certified Endocrinologists and Dermatologists. Spearmint tea is a natural dietary supplement and should complement dermatological care.
